$comment: +++===+++ 2026-11-18 16:37 +04 — Hasan Alizada — HAAL-185. Version 2 of the order of the events of one day (FR-CAL-01, F-14, D-111): the user chooses it (setting day_order) — by time, as version 1, or by colour, as the legacy app did (colour name, then title; times do not count). Two implementations (client views offline, server) against one contract.
purpose: Orders the entries shown on one day either by time (all-day first, then by start — an entry continuing from an earlier day counts as 00:00 and comes first — then by title) or by colour (by the colour's name, then by title), then by creation time and key.

key.description: Unique per entry (event id + occurrence date).

continues.description: A timed entry that started on an earlier day of the viewer.

start.description: Start on this day in the viewer's zone (HH:MM); null for all-day entries; ignored when continues.

invariants: by time — exactly version 1: every all-day entry before every timed entry; all-day entries among themselves by title; timed entries by effective start (00:00 when continues, else start), earlier first, at the same effective start a continuing entry first; the colour never takes part
by colour — the legacy order: by the colour's name in alphabetical order (black, blue, brown, green, orange, purple, red, yellow), then by title; all_day, continues and start never take part

title comparison: first by the title key — Unicode NFKD, combining marks (category M) removed, lower-cased — so case and accents do not count ("apple" < "Banana", "Eagle" < "Éclair"); then by the title itself (code points)
then by created_at (earlier first), then by key — the order is total and stable
